newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk journalist union slams media attacks.
newsitem.headline: Turk journalist union slams media attacks.

text.p: Attacks on media organisations and journalists in Turkey reached dangerous levels last month, a report by the Turkish journalists' union said on Tuesday.
Newspaper and television buildings as well as journalists were subject to armed attacks, while reporters were beaten and detained by the authorities, the report quoted by Anatolian news agency said.
"Five media organisations and two correspondents were subject to armed attacks, 11 reporters were detained and a further 24 were beated," the union's report for May said.

Demokrasi and Nu Roj, two of the few pro-Kurdish newspapers in Turkey, were closed down temporarily and the radio-television watchdog blocked broadcasts by three radio and television channels for a number of days, it said.

A student with apparent Islamist leanings last month delivered what he called "a blow to Islam", entering the headquarters of the Hurriyet newspaper, overpowering a guard and shooting a cleaner in the leg before surrendering to police.
A bomb was thrown at the same building last weekend by unknown assailants, but there were no injuries.
Armed or bomb attacks were also carried out on the privately owned national ATV and Flash TV television channels.

Anatolian quoted the report as linking the recent attacks on the secularist media with current political turmoil, fuelled by the fierce row between the country's military and the Islamist prime minister, Necmettin Erbakan.
Erbakan's government publicly accused the mainstream media of stirring up tension between ruling the Islamists and the country's secularist elite.
"Economic and...political fighting extended to attacks on the media...The events which took place in May were just like a war," the report said.
Erbakan resigned last week as a result of the row with the military.
